knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian Determinant of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}5 u \cos{\left(v \right)} \\ 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=5 u \cos{\left(v \right)}$ and $y(u,v)=5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5 \cos{\left(v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=5 \sin{\left(v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=5 u \cos{\left(v \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5 \cos{\left(v \right)}&- 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\\5 \sin{\left(v \right)}&5 u \cos{\left(v \right)}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5 \cos{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(5 u \cos{\left(v \right)}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(- 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(5 \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\\&=25 u\left(\cos^2 v+\sin^2 v\right)\\&=25 u.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian Determinant of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}u + 3 v \\ 6 u + v\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=u + 3 v$ and $y(u,v)=6 u + v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=1&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=3\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=6&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}1&3\\6&1\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(1\right)\cdot\left(1\right)-\left(3\right)\cdot\left(6\right)\\&=1-18\\&=-17.\end{aligned}
$$
